purpose: Primary-study and reference-database evidence for GrowFit cooked lamb record foodId 6. Research only; not used by enrichment, publishing, aggregation or nutrition UI.

sources.title: The Nutrient Composition of South African Lamb (A2 Class)
sources.sampleDescription: A2-class Dorper and Mutton Merino lamb from three South African production areas; cooked cut comparisons n=6.
sources.methods: Analytical composition of raw and cooked shoulder, loin and leg cuts; nutrient composition calculated for edible and trimmed lean portions.
limitations: South African breed/class and regional context may not represent GrowFit source meat
Different cut and trimming definitions yield materially different values
Not all nutrient observations are reliable; iron, zinc and B-vitamin methods are specifically cautioned in companion booklet

sources.title: The Nutrient Content of South African Lamb & Mutton
limitations: Companion booklet to South African lamb research
Authors flag selected analytical results as questionable; micronutrient rows require independent confirmation

sources.title: South African Food Data System (SAFOODS)
limitations: Public overview describes 1857 foods and selected macronutrients; exact item-level micronutrient profile not established here
Natural biological and preparation variation applies

sources.title: McCance and Widdowson's Composition of Foods Integrated Dataset 2021
limitations: UK cut/preparation definitions may not match Iranian source food
Exact food code and preparation must be verified before matching

candidates.reference: Table 3.4 cooked edible portion, meat + fat, lamb leg

reviewNotes: The two rows describe different food definitions and must not be averaged or treated as interchangeable.
GrowFit source macro values do not closely match either lamb-leg row; the 16g fat value conflicts with the trimmed-lean description.
Do not infer exact cut, trim state, or source identity from approximate macro similarity.
Micronutrient results from the booklet remain research-only because authors flag potential analytical inconsistencies, particularly iron, zinc and B vitamins.
